# Share model request capacity across Agents

Runifold 0.10.1 · Audience: application.

## Goal

Share model request capacity across Agents through the canonical runtime contracts.

## Use this API

`ModelScheduler → ProviderModelExt::scheduled → ProviderRuntime → Agent`

Dependencies / prerequisites (use the same Runifold release family):

- runifold with runtime
- One shared scheduler per local capacity domain
- Explicit positive concurrency and bounded queue limits
- Provider-aware reservation policy when token limits are configured
- Offline example: runifold-testkit, futures-util, tokio and anyhow; no credentials

## Minimal example

The following is extracted from [the compiled source](../../../crates/runifold/examples/shared_model_capacity.rs).
Excerpts may use imports, fixtures and helper types from that file; use the complete
source for a runnable example. Test-only assertions and mocks are not application setup.

```rust
use std::{
    num::{NonZeroU64, NonZeroUsize},
    time::Duration,
};

use futures_util::{StreamExt, future::try_join_all};
use runifold::{
    ContentPart, Model, ModelCallContext, ModelCapacityLimits, ModelCapacityPoolId,
    ModelEventStream, ModelRateLimit, ModelRef, ModelRequest, ModelScheduler, ModelSchedulerConfig,
    ProviderModel, ProviderModelExt, SupportLevel,
    model::{
        FeatureSupport, FinishReason, ModelCapabilities, ModelError, ModelFuture, ModelStreamEvent,
        ModelUsage,
    },
};
use runifold_testkit::ScriptedModel;

// Only the demo transport is scripted. Agent, routing, retry, and scheduling use
// the production path. A real ProviderModel can be bound identically.
struct DemoProvider(ScriptedModel);
impl ProviderModel for DemoProvider {
    fn provider(&self) -> &'static str {
        "demo"
    }
}
impl Model for DemoProvider {
    fn capabilities<'a>(
        &'a self,
        model: &'a ModelRef,
    ) -> ModelFuture<'a, Result<ModelCapabilities, ModelError>> {
        self.0.capabilities(model)
    }
    fn stream(
        &self,
        request: ModelRequest,
        context: ModelCallContext,
    ) -> ModelFuture<'_, Result<ModelEventStream, ModelError>> {
        Box::pin(async move {
            let stream = self.0.stream(request, context).await?;
            Ok(Box::pin(stream.then(|event| async move {
                tokio::task::yield_now().await;
                event
            })) as ModelEventStream)
        })
    }
}

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let account = ModelCapacityPoolId::new("research-account")?;
    let scheduler = ModelScheduler::new(
        ModelSchedulerConfig::new(NonZeroUsize::new(128).expect("positive queue bound")).pool(
            account.clone(),
            ModelCapacityLimits::new(NonZeroUsize::new(4).expect("positive concurrency")).requests(
                ModelRateLimit::new(
                    NonZeroU64::new(600).expect("positive RPM"),
                    Duration::from_secs(60),
                )?,
            ),
        )?,
    )?;
    let scripted = ScriptedModel::new().with_capabilities(ModelCapabilities {
        streaming: FeatureSupport::new(SupportLevel::Native),
        ..ModelCapabilities::default()
    });
    for _ in 0..100 {
        scripted.enqueue([
            ModelStreamEvent::ResponseStarted {
                id: None,
                model: ModelRef::new("demo", "research"),
            },
            ModelStreamEvent::ContentPartCompleted {
                index: 0,
                part: ContentPart::text("ready"),
            },
            ModelStreamEvent::UsageUpdated {
                usage: ModelUsage {
                    input_tokens: 5,
                    output_tokens: 1,
                    ..ModelUsage::default()
                },
            },
            ModelStreamEvent::ResponseCompleted {
                finish_reason: FinishReason::Stop,
                provider_metadata: std::collections::BTreeMap::new(),
            },
        ]);
    }
    // Bind the provider BEFORE runtime construction: each physical retry gets
    // its own permit. Reuse this scheduler for other models sharing the account.
    let runtime = DemoProvider(scripted)
        .scheduled(&scheduler, [account])?
        .runtime("research")?;
    let agents = (0..100)
        .map(|index| runtime.agent(format!("research-{index}")).build())
        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
    let answers = try_join_all(
        agents
            .iter()
            .map(|agent| agent.prompt_text("Research this item")),
    )
    .await?;
    assert!(answers.iter().all(|answer| answer == "ready"));
    let snapshot = scheduler.snapshot();
    assert_eq!(snapshot.admitted, 100);
    assert_eq!(snapshot.queued, 0);
    assert_eq!(snapshot.pools[0].active, 0);
    println!(
        "Completed {} Agents with shared concurrency 4; {} physical attempts admitted.",
        answers.len(),
        snapshot.admitted
    );
    Ok(())
}
```

## Production example

Construct one ModelScheduler at application startup. Bind physical providers before calling runtime so each retry reacquires capacity. Bind all account/deployment/model pools applying to a route. Configure request/token windows to match reviewed upstream constraints. Token limits require an explicit ModelTokenEstimator for billable input plus bounded output; estimates are not guaranteed upper bounds. Token settlement defaults to Conservative: it retains at least the reservation even after a terminal usage snapshot. Select ModelTokenSettlement::ReportedUsage only for adapters verified to report complete final billable input/output usage. The complete example runs 100 Agents offline without credentials. Capacity sharing and circuit health are separate scopes. Preserve the adapter runtime_profile and use without_circuit_breaker when independent tasks should not share route-health suppression, or select CircuitFailurePolicy::ServiceAvailability to count configured transport and HTTP 429/5xx failures only. Inspect runtime.profile().diagnostic_snapshot() for effective policy without private provider options. Scheduled errors expose admission/opening/waiting-first-event/streaming, separate queue/execution times and released local capacity; provider_invoked does not prove remote acceptance or cancellation. ModelError::diagnostic_metadata projects bounded operational fields for logs. Capture runifold ai environment --json for locked resolved versions and actual vendor source identities; it is separate from the runtime policy snapshot. Verify repeated release/cancellation/EOF behavior and bounded resident growth with the request_stability public test.

Compile-tested application source ([complete file](../../../crates/runifold/examples/shared_model_capacity.rs)):

//! Offline example: 100 Agents share a physical-request capacity pool.
//! Run with `cargo run -p runifold --example shared_model_capacity --locked`.
use std::{
    num::{NonZeroU64, NonZeroUsize},
    time::Duration,
};

use futures_util::{StreamExt, future::try_join_all};
use runifold::{
    ContentPart, Model, ModelCallContext, ModelCapacityLimits, ModelCapacityPoolId,
    ModelEventStream, ModelRateLimit, ModelRef, ModelRequest, ModelScheduler, ModelSchedulerConfig,
    ProviderModel, ProviderModelExt, SupportLevel,
    model::{
        FeatureSupport, FinishReason, ModelCapabilities, ModelError, ModelFuture, ModelStreamEvent,
        ModelUsage,
    },
};
use runifold_testkit::ScriptedModel;

// Only the demo transport is scripted. Agent, routing, retry, and scheduling use
// the production path. A real ProviderModel can be bound identically.
struct DemoProvider(ScriptedModel);
impl ProviderModel for DemoProvider {
    fn provider(&self) -> &'static str {
        "demo"
    }
}
impl Model for DemoProvider {
    fn capabilities<'a>(
        &'a self,
        model: &'a ModelRef,
    ) -> ModelFuture<'a, Result<ModelCapabilities, ModelError>> {
        self.0.capabilities(model)
    }
    fn stream(
        &self,
        request: ModelRequest,
        context: ModelCallContext,
    ) -> ModelFuture<'_, Result<ModelEventStream, ModelError>> {
        Box::pin(async move {
            let stream = self.0.stream(request, context).await?;
            Ok(Box::pin(stream.then(|event| async move {
                tokio::task::yield_now().await;
                event
            })) as ModelEventStream)
        })
    }
}

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let account = ModelCapacityPoolId::new("research-account")?;
    let scheduler = ModelScheduler::new(
        ModelSchedulerConfig::new(NonZeroUsize::new(128).expect("positive queue bound")).pool(
            account.clone(),
            ModelCapacityLimits::new(NonZeroUsize::new(4).expect("positive concurrency")).requests(
                ModelRateLimit::new(
                    NonZeroU64::new(600).expect("positive RPM"),
                    Duration::from_secs(60),
                )?,
            ),
        )?,
    )?;
    let scripted = ScriptedModel::new().with_capabilities(ModelCapabilities {
        streaming: FeatureSupport::new(SupportLevel::Native),
        ..ModelCapabilities::default()
    });
    for _ in 0..100 {
        scripted.enqueue([
            ModelStreamEvent::ResponseStarted {
                id: None,
                model: ModelRef::new("demo", "research"),
            },
            ModelStreamEvent::ContentPartCompleted {
                index: 0,
                part: ContentPart::text("ready"),
            },
            ModelStreamEvent::UsageUpdated {
                usage: ModelUsage {
                    input_tokens: 5,
                    output_tokens: 1,
                    ..ModelUsage::default()
                },
            },
            ModelStreamEvent::ResponseCompleted {
                finish_reason: FinishReason::Stop,
                provider_metadata: std::collections::BTreeMap::new(),
            },
        ]);
    }
    // Bind the provider BEFORE runtime construction: each physical retry gets
    // its own permit. Reuse this scheduler for other models sharing the account.
    let runtime = DemoProvider(scripted)
        .scheduled(&scheduler, [account])?
        .runtime("research")?;
    let agents = (0..100)
        .map(|index| runtime.agent(format!("research-{index}")).build())
        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
    let answers = try_join_all(
        agents
            .iter()
            .map(|agent| agent.prompt_text("Research this item")),
    )
    .await?;
    assert!(answers.iter().all(|answer| answer == "ready"));
    let snapshot = scheduler.snapshot();
    assert_eq!(snapshot.admitted, 100);
    assert_eq!(snapshot.queued, 0);
    assert_eq!(snapshot.pools[0].active, 0);
    println!(
        "Completed {} Agents with shared concurrency 4; {} physical attempts admitted.",
        answers.len(),
        snapshot.admitted
    );
    Ok(())
}

## Runtime path

Agent → ProviderRuntime/ModelRouter → physical attempt → ScheduledModel atomic admission → provider stream → settlement and release

Preserve the owning crate's canonical execution and authority checks. The full
source linked above provides the executable context; related contracts explain
production persistence and failure boundaries.

## Do not do this

- Do not create independent schedulers for routes sharing an upstream quota.
- Do not wrap a retrying router when physical-attempt accounting is required.
- Do not confuse execution Token budgets with rate limits, or assume an estimate guarantees the provider TPM ceiling.
- Do not claim process-local admission coordinates other processes or proves remote cancellation.
- Do not infer complete final usage merely because a stream emitted UsageUpdated; partial snapshots must not authorize refunds.
